documents.content:
# Python HTTP API
The synthetic backend uses Python and FastAPI for HTTP request validation and response schemas. API handlers persist user intent without running the long agent workflow.

# Async relational storage
The synthetic persistence layer uses async PostgreSQL connections and SQLAlchemy sessions. Short transactions store business facts; model network calls run outside transactions.

# Deterministic testing
The synthetic test suite injects fake model and search ports. Fixed inputs and expected assertions make offline unit tests repeatable without provider credentials.

# Docker deployment
The synthetic deployment packages API and one worker with Docker Compose on a Linux host. Caddy terminates ingress; migrations are a separate operator command.

# LangGraph state and routing
The synthetic LangGraph graph passes typed State between plan, research, validate and writer nodes. Conditional routing uses evidence sufficiency to choose a bounded next step.

# Bounded agent loop
The synthetic research loop limits model turns and tool calls. A deterministic guard stops additional proposals when its declared run budget is exhausted.

# Checkpoint and resume
The synthetic checkpoint stores graph recovery state. After restart, the executor resumes the saved node state; public APIs still read PostgreSQL business records.

# Human approval interrupt
The synthetic HITL flow interrupts before submission. A reviewer approves the exact argument binding, and the worker resumes from the persisted approval decision.

# Normalize and chunk
The synthetic ingestion normalizes Unicode to NFC and newlines to LF. Markdown headings and paragraphs determine immutable chunks bounded by an 800-byte UTF-8 budget.

# Embedding vectors
The synthetic retrieval pipeline embeds text into 1536-dimensional vectors with text-embedding-v4. PostgreSQL pgvector exact cosine search ranks compatible embedding profiles.

# Workspace and document filtering
The synthetic retrieval query applies workspace identity and an explicit document allowlist before selecting top five chunks. A foreign workspace document stays excluded even if its ID appears in caller input.

# Untrusted retrieved instructions
Synthetic RAG chunks are untrusted evidence. Citations identify document and chunk IDs; instructions inside a chunk cannot change the system policy or trusted execution context.

# Registry input schema
The synthetic Tool Registry declares each tool name, effect and strict input schema. Unknown tools and malformed argument proposals are rejected before handler execution.

# Trusted execution context
The synthetic ToolExecutionContext is constructed by trusted code. Workspace, actor, target, credentials and approval binding never come from model tool arguments.

# Timeout and retry limits
The synthetic tool handler has a deadline and bounded timeout policy. Retry follows typed transient failures and declared attempt limits rather than unbounded automatic retries.

# Irreversible idempotency
The synthetic irreversible submission binds immutable args and target to exact approval. Repeated attempts reuse a stable idempotency key so the external Mock Portal converges.

# Lease and at-least-once delivery
The synthetic single worker claims jobs with an expiring lease. Reclaim can redeliver work at least once, so stable identities and conditional writes make execution converge.

# Cancellation
The synthetic worker checks cancellation before new model and tool work. A revoked workspace membership also cancels the run; an already executing external action requires reconciliation.

# Typed failure handling
The synthetic domain raises typed failures with safe categories. HTTP boundaries map them to problem details without leaking provider errors or business text into logs.

# Unknown external outcome
The synthetic outcome_unknown status means submission may have happened but confirmation is missing. Automatic POST retries stop after bounded reconciliation, and the operator investigates.

# Deterministic regression baseline
The synthetic offline regression compares versioned fake-eval artifacts against an accepted baseline. Ordinary CI reports drift and never refreshes accepted evidence automatically.

# Live eval fixed evidence
The synthetic live evaluation holds web and document evidence fixed while the real chat model varies. Preselected cases and repeat counts prevent rerolling until a passing sample appears.

# Agent Trace Tree
The synthetic Trace Tree relates execution segments, graph nodes, tools, retrieval and model attempts. Langfuse is a lossy observation copy and never owns workflow state.

# Tokens cost and latency
The synthetic accounting records tokens, known cost and elapsed milliseconds for every provider attempt. Unknown prices remain unknown; observed sample p50 and p95 do not establish a production latency guarantee.

# Excluded duplicate
The synthetic backend uses Python and FastAPI for HTTP validation. SAME_WORKSPACE_EXCLUDED_CANARY must not be returned because this document is outside the allowed document list.

# Workspace and document filtering
The synthetic retrieval query applies workspace identity and an explicit document allowlist before selecting top five chunks. A foreign workspace document stays excluded even if its ID appears in caller input. FOREIGN_WORKSPACE_CANARY must never appear in retrieved primary-workspace results.

queries.query: Which language and web framework validate HTTP requests?
How does the backend use asynchronous relational database sessions?
How can unit tests run repeatably without any model provider key?
How is typed state passed and routed among LangGraph nodes?
What restores graph progress after a process restart?
How does human review interrupt and resume a submission?
How are Unicode, line endings and Markdown sections normalized into chunks?
Which vector dimension and storage extension support cosine retrieval?
How are workspace identity and document allowlists applied before top five retrieval?
Can instructions found inside a cited document chunk override trusted policy?
What rejects unknown tools or malformed argument proposals before execution?
Who sets the workspace, actor and target in ToolExecutionContext?
How are tool timeouts and transient retries bounded?
What keeps repeated approved irreversible submissions from duplicating the external effect?
Why can a worker receive the same job again after its lease expires?
When does a worker stop new work after cancellation or membership revocation?
What happens when an external submission may have succeeded but cannot be confirmed?
Does ordinary offline CI replace the accepted fake-eval baseline when results change?
How are model attempts and tools related to graph nodes in observability?
How are tokens, unknown cost and observed latency percentiles recorded for provider attempts?
